questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the front and rear axles on a wheel-type machine?
options: To transfer power from the drive shafts to the tires to drive and stop the machine
questions.explanation: Axles transfer power from the drive shafts to the tires to both drive and stop the machine.

questions.prompt: Inboard axles are found on which machines?
options: Small and medium wheel loaders and backhoe loaders
questions.explanation: Inboard axles are on small and medium wheel loaders and backhoe loaders; outboard axles on the large machines.

questions.prompt: What does the bevel gear set do?
options: Gives the final reduction at the wheel
Receives power from the drive shaft, turns it 90 degrees and sends it to the differential
questions.explanation: The bevel pinion and ring gear turn the power flow 90 degrees to the differential.

questions.prompt: What does the differential do?
options: Provides a balance of power to the wheels and transfers power to the final drives
questions.explanation: The differential balances power between the wheels, which is needed during turns.

questions.prompt: In the differential, what do the pinion (spider) gears do?
options: Transmit power from the differential case to the side gears
questions.explanation: The pinion gears ride on the spider and transmit power from the case to the side gears.

questions.prompt: What provides the last speed reduction and torque increase in a wheel machine drivetrain?
questions.explanation: The planetary group is the final drive: last speed reduction and torque increase.

questions.prompt: In an inboard axle planetary group, the ring gear...
options: Is pressed into the axle housing and does not rotate
Is splined to the sun shaft
questions.explanation: The ring gear is held in the housing; the sun shaft drives the planet gears.

questions.prompt: What retracts the service brake piston when hydraulic pressure is released?
questions.explanation: Springs, always under compression, retract the piston when pressure drops.

questions.prompt: Wheel speed brakes are used on...
options: Off-highway trucks and some large wheel loaders
questions.explanation: The wheel speed brake is used in off-highway trucks and some large wheel loaders.

questions.prompt: When is a double reduction planetary final drive used?
questions.explanation: Double reduction planetary groups give the final reduction on some larger machines.

questions.prompt: Why are traction aids needed?
options: Because the outside wheel travels further than the inside wheel in a turn, and a slipping wheel can take all the power
questions.explanation: An open differential lets wheels turn at different speeds, so a wheel with no traction spins while the other stops.

questions.prompt: What does a NoSPIN differential do?
options: Forces both wheels to turn at the same speed regardless of traction
questions.explanation: NoSPIN is an automatic locking differential that drives both wheels at the same speed.

questions.prompt: A Limited Slip Differential gives equal power to both wheels until...
options: Ground conditions between the left and right wheels differ
questions.explanation: The LSD shares power equally until underfoot conditions differ side to side.

questions.prompt: How does a multi-disc differential lock differ from a jaw clutch lock?
options: It can only engage when stopped
It can engage under full power independent of wheel spin
questions.explanation: The jaw clutch engages only when wheels turn at the same speed; the multi-disc lock engages under full power regardless of wheel spin.

questions.prompt: How does the wheel loader Traction Control System (TCS) give traction assist?
options: By using the brakes on the slipping wheel, sending torque to the wheel with the best traction
questions.explanation: TCS behaves like an open differential and uses the brakes to transfer torque to the wheel with traction.

questions.prompt: Which inputs does the TCS use to decide on wheel speed ratio?
options: Four wheel speed sensors and an articulation sensor
questions.explanation: TCS reads four wheel speed sensors and an articulation angle sensor.

questions.prompt: Which brakes does the Automatic Electronic Traction Aid (AETA) on trucks use?
questions.explanation: AETA uses the rear parking brakes (spring engaged, hydraulically released) to slow a spinning wheel.

questions.prompt: How is a track-type machine steered?
options: By causing one track to turn faster than the other
questions.explanation: A track machine steers by making one track turn faster than the other.

questions.prompt: Which two lower drivetrain systems are used on track-type tractors?
questions.explanation: Track-type tractors use either the steering clutch system or the differential steer system.

questions.prompt: Track-type tractor brakes are typically...
options: Oil-cooled multiple disc, spring applied and hydraulically released
questions.explanation: The brakes are oil-cooled multi-disc, spring applied (Belleville springs) and hydraulically released.

questions.prompt: What do the steering clutches do?
options: Transfer power from the bevel gears to the final drives and turn the machine
questions.explanation: The steering clutches transfer power to the final drives; releasing one turns the machine.

questions.prompt: In the differential steer system, what drives the steer planetary?
options: The steering motor through a bevel pinion and ring gear
questions.explanation: The steering motor drives the steer planetary; the transmission drives the drive planetary.

questions.prompt: Why can a differential steer tractor still turn with the transmission in neutral?
options: Because of the speed difference generated by the steering motor
questions.explanation: In neutral the steering motor still drives through the differential, so the tractor can counter-rotate the tracks.

questions.prompt: What is a hydrostatic drive system?
options: A closed-loop hydraulic system that gives infinitely variable travel speeds
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic drive is a closed loop that converts mechanical power to hydraulic and back to mechanical power.

questions.prompt: In a hydrostatic drive, what determines the pressure in the drive line?
options: The load on the drive motor
questions.explanation: Pressure in the drive line is determined by the load on the drive motor.

questions.prompt: What is the job of the charge pump in a hydrostatic drive?
options: To supply make-up oil to the drive loop
To control the swashplate angle directly
questions.explanation: The charge pump supplies oil to the propel pump and provides make-up oil to the loop.

questions.prompt: What do the crossover and main relief valves protect against?
options: Excessive high pressure spikes in the propel system
questions.explanation: The crossover and main relief valves protect the propel system from high pressure spikes.

questions.prompt: What changes the displacement of a variable displacement piston pump?
options: The swashplate angle, moved by the servo
questions.explanation: Moving the control lever moves the servo, which changes the swashplate angle and so the pump output.

questions.prompt: On a hydraulic excavator travel motor, how is the parking brake released?
options: By pump oil acting on the parking brake piston
questions.explanation: Springs apply the parking brake; pump oil on the parking brake piston releases it.

questions.prompt: When the straight travel valve is activated on an excavator, what happens?
options: One pump's flow goes to both travel control valves so the machine tracks straight while implements are used
questions.explanation: The straight travel valve crosses flow so one pump feeds both travel valves and the other feeds the implements.
